data.title: Elder Financial Exploitation — New Payee Addition with Escalating Payment Amounts
data.description: Detects a multi-signal elder financial exploitation pattern: account holder aged 65 or older adds a new payee not present in their historical payment network, followed by escalating payment amounts to that payee over a rolling 30-day window. FBI IC3 reported $7.748B in elder fraud losses in 2025 (59% YoY increase from $4.885B in 2024), with 201,266 complaints from victims aged 60+. Crypto ATM/kiosk fraud disproportionately targets this cohort: 6,188 complaints and $257M in losses from 60+ victims alone. The convergence of advanced age, new payee addition, and escalating amounts is a hallmark of romance scams, tech support fraud, government impersonation, and caregiver exploitation — all of which follow a pattern of trust-building followed by increasing financial extraction. This rule targets Phase 4 (Execution) but the escalating pattern often indicates prolonged Phase 2/3 social engineering that has already been underway for weeks or months.

enrichment_required.source: Days since payee first appeared in account holder's transaction history
Boolean flag indicating whether payee exists in 12-month historical payment network
Trend analysis (increasing/stable/decreasing) of payment amounts to this payee over the rolling window

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Elder Exploitation — New Payee with Escalating Payments
// Detects account holders 65+ sending escalating amounts to new payees
account_holder_age>=65
payee_first_seen_days<=30
payee_in_historical_pattern=false
| payment_count := count(payment_id)
| groupBy(account_id, payee_id, function=[
    collect([account_holder_age, payee_name, payment_method]),
    count(payment_id, as=payment_count),
    sum(payment_amount, as=total_amount),
    min(payment_amount, as=first_payment),
    max(payment_amount, as=largest_payment)
  ])
| payment_count >= 3
| escalation_ratio := largest_payment / first_payment
| escalation_ratio > 1.5
| sort(total_amount, order=desc)
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Elder Exploitation — New Payee with Escalating Payments")`
`comment("Detects account holders 65+ with escalating payments to new payees")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:transaction_monitoring
  account_holder_age>=65
  payee_first_seen_days<=30
  payee_in_historical_pattern="false"
| sort 0 account_id, payee_id, payment_date
| streamstats count AS payment_seq, sum(payment_amount) AS running_total,
    first(payment_amount) AS first_payment, last(payment_amount) AS latest_payment
    by account_id, payee_id
| where payment_seq >= 3
| eval escalation_ratio = latest_payment / first_payment
| where escalation_ratio > 1.5
| eval risk_score = case(
    escalation_ratio > 5 AND running_total > 50000, "critical",
    escalation_ratio > 3 OR running_total > 25000, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| stats max(payment_seq) AS payment_count, max(running_total) AS total_amount,
    min(first_payment) AS first_payment, max(latest_payment) AS largest_payment,
    max(escalation_ratio) AS escalation_ratio, values(risk_score) AS risk_score
    by account_id, account_holder_age, payee_id, payee_name
| sort - total_amount
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Elder Exploitation — New Payee with Escalating Payments
-- Detects escalating payment pattern from elderly account holders to new payees
WITH payee_payments AS (
  SELECT
    t.account_id,
    c.account_holder_age,
    t.payee_id,
    t.payee_name,
    t.payment_amount,
    t.payment_date,
    t.payment_method,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id, t.payee_id ORDER BY t.payment_date) AS payment_seq,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id, t.payee_id) AS payment_count,
    SUM(t.payment_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id, t.payee_id) AS total_amount,
    FIRST_VALUE(t.payment_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id, t.payee_id ORDER BY t.payment_date) AS first_payment,
    MAX(t.payment_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id, t.payee_id) AS largest_payment
  FROM transactions t
  JOIN customer_demographics c ON t.account_id = c.account_id
  LEFT JOIN historical_payee_network h ON t.account_id = h.account_id AND t.payee_id = h.payee_id
  WHERE c.account_holder_age >= 65
    AND t.payment_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -30, CURRENT_DATE)
    AND h.payee_id IS NULL  -- payee not in historical pattern
)
SELECT
  account_id,
  account_holder_age,
  payee_id,
  payee_name,
  payment_count,
  total_amount,
  first_payment,
  largest_payment,
  ROUND(largest_payment / NULLIF(first_payment, 0), 2) AS escalation_ratio
FROM payee_payments
WHERE payment_seq = payment_count  -- latest row per group
  AND payment_count >= 3
  AND largest_payment > first_payment * 1.5
ORDER BY total_amount DESC

falsepositives: Legitimate new service providers (home repair, medical) with naturally increasing invoice amounts
Recurring charitable donations with annual increases
Family members newly added as payees receiving regular support payments
Home healthcare or assisted living payments that increase with care level changes
